what: What did each Lunenburg town employee earn in 1991?
why: `report-gross-wages` holds per-employee earnings from the 2010 report (calendar wages) and FY2011-FY2025 (fiscal). The 1991 annual town report prints no wage list: its text (68 pages, every page) was searched for wage, gross, earning, salary, payroll and compensation and returned only appropriation lines for officers' salaries (p25, p27, p28), the omnibus lines (p46), the Treasurer's count `Persons on payroll 411` (p30), and the Article 17 salary-schedule vote (p48) -- no list by employee (sources/data/report-tables/1991/). — closes: the Town's calendar-1991 payroll register (W-2 totals by employee) from the Treasurer's office.

what: What were the town's non-union salary grades and step rates in fiscal 1992?
why: `salary-schedule` and `report-classification-plan` read Schedule A from the 2010 report and FY2011 onward. The 1991 annual town report records the vote but not the schedule: Article 17 of the May 11, 1991 Annual Town Meeting replaced `the Classification and Salary Schedule voted on May 12, 1990` with the one `proposed by the Personnel Committee and appearing in the report of the Finance Committee`, effective July 1, 1991, with $19,078 from free cash -- VOTED (p48). The text was searched for salary schedule, classification, step and grade and returned only that article and school grade levels (sources/data/report-tables/1991/). — closes: the Finance Committee's report to the May 11, 1991 Annual Town Meeting, which printed the Classification & Salary Schedule.

what: What did each special revenue fund take in, spend and carry forward in fiscal 1991?
why: `special-revenue-funds` holds forward, receipts, disbursements and balance by fund from the 2001-2010 reports. The 1991 annual town report prints no special revenue schedule: the only special revenue figures are the balance sheet's SPECIAL REVENUE column, $89,233 of cash and the same amount designated (p23). The text was searched for special revenue, revolving and grant and returned department prose about grants (p6, p10, p13, p15, p21) and the trust accounts' GRANTS & GIFTS column (p36-p39) (sources/data/report-tables/1991/). — closes: the Town Accountant's fiscal 1991 special revenue fund ledger (or the Schedule A filed with the Department of Revenue for FY1991).

what: What was appropriated, spent and carried forward on each capital project fund in fiscal 1991?
why: `report-capital-projects` holds a separate capital project fund schedule from the 2001-2010 reports. The 1991 annual town report prints none, and its balance sheet has no capital projects column (p23). Capital articles appear INSIDE the general fund appropriations schedule instead -- e.g. `13/90 Fire Dept. Pumper` $180,000 (p26), `2/91 Sunset Lane Betterment` and `12/90 Traffic Signals` (p27) -- so whether any borrowing-funded project sat in a separate fund is not shown. Searched for capital project and capital fund (sources/data/report-tables/1991/). — closes: the Town Accountant's fiscal 1991 capital projects fund ledger.

what: What did each item of Lunenburg's FY1992 capital plan cost?
why: `capital-plans` holds item-by-item costs. The 1991 annual town report prints no capital plan: the Capital Planning Committee's report says the Committee `was formed in September of` 1991 and that its first task is to establish a procedure for capital requests (p18-p19), and Article 29 of the May 11, 1991 ATM, putting the Committee into a by-law, prints no amounts (p50). Searched for capital (sources/data/report-tables/1991/). — closes: the Capital Planning Committee's first capital plan (FY1993), or the Finance Committee's FY1992 report listing capital articles.

what: How much of Lunenburg's debt at 30 June 1991 sat inside the debt limit, and how much outside it?
why: `outstanding-debt` reads this from the five-year outstanding-debt summary the FY2011-FY2025 reports print. The 1991 annual town report prints its bonded indebtedness issue by issue (PDF page 32) and a repayment schedule (p33-p34) whose interest lines mark four issues `INTEREST (EXEMPTED)`, but no summary by purpose and no debt-limit split: its text was searched for debt limit, outstanding and indebtedness and returned only those headings and the index (p67). — closes: the Town's FY1991 Statement of Indebtedness as filed with the Division of Local Services.

what: What was Lunenburg's assessed valuation by property class, its levy, overlay and new growth for fiscal 1991?
why: `report-valuation` holds the Assessors' tables (assessments by class, valuation and tax history, abstract by class code, overlay, new growth) from the 2001 and 2010 reports and FY2011 onward. The 1991 annual town report prints none of them: the Board of Assessors' report is prose and a list of exemption clauses (p8-p9), and the only valuation figures are in ABOUT THE TOWN, `$481,456,703-Real Estate`, `$12,165,184-Personal Prop.`, `TAX RATE: $13.18 (Fiscal 1992)` (p3) -- a year LATER than the book's accounts. Searched for valuation, overlay, tax rate, new growth, levy and assessment (sources/data/report-tables/1991/). — closes: the Assessors' FY1991 tax rate recapitulation (Form LA-4/recap) filed with the Department of Revenue.

what: How many weighing and measuring devices did the Sealer test in 1991, and what did sealing bring in by device?
why: `report-weights-measures` holds the Sealer's device counts and fees from the 2010 report. The 1991 annual town report prints only a paragraph: `twenty-four visits were made to Town businesses with a total of $648.00 collected in fees` (p21), against the receipts line SEALING FEES $692.00 (p24) -- the two figures differ and nothing on either page reconciles them. Searched for weights, sealer and sealing (sources/data/report-tables/1991/). — closes: the Sealer of Weights and Measures' 1991 annual report to the Division of Standards.
